key_insight: A symmetry-preserving neural density functional can learn ion correlations in polymer electrolytes and transfer them across concentrations, geometries, and length scales.
engineering_relevance: This enables more reliable continuum-scale prediction of electrolyte structure and response from molecular data, which is useful for designing batteries and other ion-conducting materials.
method: Trained a neural density functional on planar density and internal-force profiles from molecular dynamics.
Built in spatial symmetries, thermodynamic integrability, and Noether identities to preserve physics.
Used the model to predict density profiles, bulk structure factors, and long-wavelength number response in unseen settings.
evidence_signal: From the abstract, the model was trained only on planar MD data and still predicted an untrained salt concentration, larger domains, and 2D external fields more accurately than three alternative architectures.
watch_item: Transferability is promising, but performance may depend on staying within stable, noncritical regimes where perfect screening and the learned correlations remain valid.
paper_title: A structure-preserving neural density functional for the ions of a polymer electrolyte
